sections.title: Talking About the Weather
sections.content: Spanish does not say it is hot — it says it makes heat. Most weather runs on 'hace' plus a noun: hace calor, hace sol, hace frío. Rain and snow get their own verbs, used only in this one form: llueve, nieva. And a state of the sky takes 'está': está nublado. Three patterns, and every forecast you need is one of them.

items.spanish: El cielo está muy gris. Creo que va a llover.
items.english: The sky is very grey. I think it's going to rain.

items.spanish: En mi país hace mucho calor en esta época del año.
items.english: In my country it's very hot at this time of year.

items.spanish: Por la tarde sale el sol otra vez.
items.english: In the afternoon the sun comes out again.

sections.content: 'Hace calor' is the weather; 'tengo calor' is you. Spanish keeps them apart with different verbs, so 'estoy caliente' is not the sentence you want — say 'tengo calor'.

sections.topic: the verb 'hacer', which carries the weather
